identity_notes: No large single-ingredient RCT of isolated dandelion (leaf, root, or whole herb) exists for the most commonly marketed label claims (diuretic, digestive/liver support). The single clean single-agent human RCT in this scope (PMID 42398668) is a small (n=14), single-dose, acute crossover trial that found NO diuretic effect -- directly contradicting the traditional/marketed diuretic claim. Most other kept efficacy records are MULTI-INGREDIENT combination products (BNO 1030/Imupret, turmeric+dandelion+milk-thistle+ginger liver nutraceuticals, compound dandelion soup, glycyrrhizinate+dandelion for paraquat poisoning, herbal detox tea) where dandelion's individual contribution cannot be isolated from the abstract data -- these were kept but flagged related_form_differs/combination:true throughout. Applicability caveat requested by the brief: the 'Pugongying granules' extract used for lactational mastitis (PMID 38029215) and the compound-dandelion-soup sore-throat formulations (PMID 22419300) are China-specific patented/traditional preparations, not generic 'dandelion extract' as typically labeled on US supplement products. Retrieved literature is dominated by dandelion-as-a-plant environmental/agronomy studies (heavy metal/microplastic stress response) and in vitro or animal mechanistic work, all rejected as off_topic/animal_or_invitro. Safety signal: dandelion is a known Compositae/Asteraceae contact allergen (2 case series, PMID 1838315 and 3827282), relevant to any handoff safety review given dandelion's frequent co-labeling with other Asteraceae botanicals.
